title: Prove a pair-sum readout floor for partitioned walk duals at every Q (no new κ)
body:
## Result

**Scoped proof and finite certificate in the PR1898 abstract tariff; no new κ.** Package: `research/partitioned-walk-pair-sum-floor/`.

This answers open question 2 of Wentao Li's #2779 (`research/independent-walks-7q-obstruction`): repeated labels inside a partitioned walk never cover at `Q=7`. Covering needs `Σ(n_i−1) ≥ 5`, and at `Q=7` this is tight, so each walk must have independent labels. PR #2779's `R=112` is therefore the exact minimum over all label patterns.

For any labels (repeats and interior zero revisits allowed) and any number of walks, the cost-2 masks are pair sums of one walk. This gives

```text
R ≥ max(62, 122 − (Q−2)(Q−3)).
```

The floor is attained at `Q=8` (`R=92`, walks `(0,10)`, `(0,22,5,31,24,20)`) and `Q=9` (`R=80`, walks `(0,3)`, `(0,18,1,5,11,20,27)`). The tariff floor `38Q+2R` is at least 470 at every `Q ≥ 7`. No partitioned independent dual undercuts the six-query endpoint tariff 436 at any query count.

## Evidence and reproduction

`verify.py` imports PR #2779's `model.py` (pinned live input). It checks:

- the table lemma (finite iff in span; cost 2 iff pair sum) on all 924,482 restored walks of length 2–5;
- the `Q=7` rank census: 624,960 of 894,660 length-5 walks and 26,040 of 28,861 length-4 walks have full rank, all with distinct nonzero labels;
- 4,000 seeded random duals with `Q` from 7 to 11, of which 2,456 cover, against both floors and against #2779's two-port dual;
- the witnesses and the tariff floors.

```sh
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B research/partitioned-walk-pair-sum-floor/verify.py
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/partitioned-walk-pair-sum-floor
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/partitioned-walk-pair-sum-floor --check-source-history
```

All three passed locally (Python 3.12, about 25 s for the verifier).

## Limitations

- The result is stated in the abstract tariff only. It is not a physical supplier and not a multiplication theorem.
- The `k ≥ 3` walk cost is the natural min-plus extension of the two-port dual. No earlier package defines it.
- Same-walk, transfer-coupled and shared-dirt schedules are out of scope.
- The random controls are sanity checks; the floor rests on the written proof. Independent human and formal review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

1. What are the exact minima at `Q=10, 11`? The floor gives 66 and 62; a seeded search found 72 and 66.
2. Can a pair-sum count with the shared prefix charged once bound transfer-coupled duals at every `Q`?

## Related open work

- #2817 (transfer-coupled (5,1,1) at `Q=7`) studies the same readout in the transfer-coupled interface. That interface is outside this package's scope, so no number is compared.
